intro: The Mishnah was short. The book that grew around it is huge. In this unit you will meet the rabbis who made it. Some lived by a lake in Galilee. Some lived by a river in Babylon, in the land that is now Iraq. For about three hundred years they asked questions about the Mishnah, and their discussion became the Gemara.

Then you will open the book itself. You will learn what a daf is, why every tractate starts on page 2, and who all the people are whose words crowd the edges of the page. You will meet Rashi, who lived in France, and his grandsons, who loved to find contradictions. You will meet a printer in Venice and a family of printers in Vilna.

By the end you will be able to read a citation like Berakhot 2a and find the page, in a book or on a free website. You will know why there are two Talmuds and which one people usually mean. And you will know why, on any morning, people in Chicago, Denver and Jerusalem can all be reading the same page.
bigQuestion: How did the Mishnah grow into the Talmud, and how does one page hold so many voices?

timeline.t: Rabbi Judah the Prince finishes the Mishnah in the Land of Israel
Rav goes to Babylonia and founds the academy at Sura
Nehardea is destroyed; Pumbedita becomes a great academy
Abaye and Rava argue at Pumbedita
The Jerusalem Talmud is finished, mostly in Tiberias
Rav Ashi of Sura dies; tradition calls him and Ravina the end of instruction
The Babylonian Talmud is mostly complete; the Savoraim add notes
Rashi lives in Troyes, France, and writes his commentary
Daniel Bomberg prints the whole Babylonian Talmud in Venice
The Romm press prints the Vilna edition, the standard page
Rabbi Meir Shapiro begins Daf Yomi, one page a day

the Mishnah and the Gemara together; the word means "learning"
a rabbi of the Gemara; the plural is amoraim
the academy in Babylonia founded by Rav around 219 CE
the academy in Babylonia famous for Abaye and Rava
the Jerusalem Talmud, finished around 400 CE, made mostly in Tiberias

one leaf of the Talmud, with sides a and b

choices: The first five books of the Bible
The rabbis' discussion of the Mishnah
test.why: The Gemara is the long discussion of the Mishnah by the amoraim, from about 200 to 500 CE.

test.q: Which two lands were home to the rabbis of the Gemara?
choices: The Land of Israel and Babylonia
test.why: The Gemara was made in Galilee, in the Land of Israel, and in Babylonia, today's Iraq.

test.q: What language is most of the Gemara in?
test.why: The Gemara is mostly in Aramaic, the everyday language of the time; the Mishnah is in Hebrew.

test.q: Who founded the academy at Sura?
test.why: Rav brought the Mishnah to Babylonia around 219 CE and founded the school at Sura.

choices: Famous arguing partners at Pumbedita in the 300s
test.why: Abaye and Rava of Pumbedita debated on hundreds of pages of the Gemara.

test.q: Which Talmud was finished first, and about when?
test.why: The Yerushalmi was finished around 400 CE; the Bavli about a century later, around 500 CE.

test.q: Which Talmud do people usually mean when they say "the Talmud"?
test.why: The Bavli is longer and became the main book of Jewish law and study.
A citation gives the tractate, the leaf and the side: a is the front, b is the back.

test.q: Which commentary sits on the inside edge of the page, near the fold?
test.why: Rashi's explanation is on the inside edge; the Tosafot are on the outside edge.
The Tosafot were written in France and Germany in the 1100s and 1200s by Rashi's grandsons and students.

choices: Printed the first complete Babylonian Talmud in Venice
test.why: Bomberg, a Christian printer in Venice, printed the whole Bavli between 1520 and 1523.

test.q: Where was the standard edition of the Talmud printed in the 1880s?
test.why: The Romm press in Vilna, today's Vilnius, printed the standard page between 1880 and 1886.

choices: A celebration for finishing a book
The first order of the Mishnah
Reading one daf of Talmud each day, everywhere, on the same schedule
test.why: Daf Yomi, "the daily page," was begun in 1923 by Rabbi Meir Shapiro.

test.q: About how long does it take to finish the whole Babylonian Talmud in Daf Yomi?
choices: About seven and a half years
test.why: The Bavli has 2,711 leaves, one per day, so a cycle takes about seven years and five months.

test.q: The Gemara keeps the question, the proof, the objection and the answer. What does the Talmud value that shows?
choices: The whole argument, including the side that lost
test.why: The Gemara keeps every step and every voice, so readers can follow the path and hear the minority.

write.prompt: Why did the rabbis keep the whole argument on the page, and not just the answer? Use Bava Metzia 84a (Rabbi Yochanan and Resh Lakish), Ta'anit 7a (learning from friends and students) and Bekhorot 49b (deciding between Rav and Shmuel). Say what each passage says, and how readers have used it.
tips: Name the tractate and page for every passage you use.
Say "the Gemara says" or "Rabbi Yochanan said," so every idea has its speaker.
Describe what the passage protects: a partner's right to object, a student's question.
Compare two readers of the same passage instead of saying who is right.
Use the unit's words: Gemara, amora, daf, chavruta.
